info.description:
Multi-tenant Identity and Access Management.

This API has two independent Bearer-token systems. Both use the same
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, but the tokens are NOT interchangeable:

- **Admin console** (every tag below not prefixed `public-app-`): an HS256 JWT
issued by the admin login flow, scoped via strings like `organizations:read`,
`applications:write`, `super:admin`. Manages organizations, workspaces,
applications, and admin users.

- **Per-application public API** (tags prefixed `public-app-`, routes under
`/public/applications/{id}/...`): an RS256 JWT signed with that *specific
application's own keypair*, scoped via that application's own
`application_user_acl.roles` (e.g. `users:read`, `scopes:write`). A token
minted for one application returns 401 against any other application's
`{id}` — these are end-user tokens for that one app, never admin credentials.

post.description:
Runs a live GeoIP lookup for this episode's IP and persists the result into
geoip_info — for historical episodes recorded before the GeoIP feature existed.
Fails with 409 if geoip_info is already set (never overwrites an existing frozen
snapshot) or if GeoIP is not currently enabled. matched:false (still 200) means the
IP is loopback/private or has no current GeoLite2 coverage — nothing is persisted,
so the button stays available for a future retry.

post.description:
Re-applies every currently-active (non-expired) ip_bans row through the same
Ban() path a fresh ban already uses — useful after a host reboot or manual firewall
flush. Already-loaded IPs are safely re-applied, not duplicated at the DB level.
post.summary: Resync active IP bans into the OS-level firewall

get.description:
Returns the IPs currently blocked at the OS firewall level, read live from the
backend in use (iptables/pf) — informational; /admin/security/ip-bans remains the
source of truth for what should be banned.

delete.description:
Removes every OS-level rule for ip — there may be more than one if Ban() was called
repeatedly for an already-banned IP. If ip is still actively banned in
/admin/security/ip-bans, that ban row is deleted too: removing an IP from this page
means fully unbanning it, not leaving a rule that would just reappear on the next
resync. Requires both admin:security:firewall:write (route-level) and
admin:security:ipbans:write (checked here), since this can delete an ip_bans row —
mirrors IPBanAccountsHandler's pattern of an additional in-handler scope check beyond
the route's own gate.

FailureReason is one of invalid_credentials, inactive_user,
no_scopes, mfa_required, mfa_failed — empty on success.
mfa_required is a provisional outcome (password was correct,
MFA verification still pending), not a hard failure.

geoip_info.description:
GeoIPInfo is a JSON snapshot of the country/city/ISP resolved
for ip at record time — empty when the IP was loopback/private,
GeoIP had no coverage, GeoIP is disabled, or the row predates
this field. Never re-derived later. See
plan/login-log-geoip/plan.md.

allow_password_login.description:
AllowPasswordLogin toggles the username+password login endpoint
for this app. Default true preserves legacy behaviour; an admin
flips it off to force the OAuth-only path. Both the login
handler and the public auth-methods endpoint honour this flag.

registration_type.description:
RegistrationType declares how registration is collected:
  - "legacy": consumers render a form with username + password
    implicit and the admin-configured extras on top.
  - "oauth":  provider delivers identity; extras only.
Only "legacy" is wired today; "oauth" is a declarative label
we surface so the consumer can branch its UI ahead of the
provider-flow implementation landing.

application_user_id.description:
ApplicationUserID is empty when the typed username never
resolved to a real end-user account.

failure_reason.description:
FailureReason is one of invalid_credentials, inactive_user, or
empty on success. inactive_user covers the application-level
password-login-disabled rejection, not just an inactive user
account.

resource_ids.description:
ResourceIDs is an opaque JSON-encoded array of ids this scope is
constrained to. Defaults to "[]" (unconstrained) when omitted.

scope_id.description:
ScopeID must match acl.ScopeIDFormat: letters/underscores per
segment, separated by colons. Immutable once created.

file_url.description:
FileURL is the absolute serve URL for file-type fields that have a
stored value. Empty for non-file fields and for file fields with no
uploaded file. Populated by PopulateFileURLs after BuildResponse.

value.description:
Value is the user's current value for this field, or null
when the user hasn't filled it in. Type follows DataType:
text → string, number → float64, date → string, select → string, etc.
